newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on physical buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on physical buying.

text.p: A marginal increase in physical demand pushed up prices in Hong Kong on Friday and spot gold ended slightly higher than New York's Thursday close, but end users still feared price falls, bullion dealers said.
"The market just looks bad after gold's overnight fall and people are afraid to do anything," said a gold trader at an international bank's office in the British colony.
Some traders reported professional sales and rumours of Australian producer buy-backs were heard but these could not be confirmed.
With next week shortened in New York by the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday, Hong Kong traders foresaw a quiet market recovering from the steep drop.
"I think it's just going to take a rest," said one dealer.
Bullion ended at US$376.65/377.15 an ounce on Friday against New York's US$376.30/80 close on Thursday.
Gold slid overnight in New York, ending on Thursday at its lowest level since March 1995 on producer hedging and fund selling, traders said.
Local gold ended HK$9 lower at HK$3,476 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at -5.00.
